title: burst-probe-econ-scan-apr30-2026
content:
Objective:
Run a lightweight field scan that compares monetary cost and tail/median latency when we exercise short, repeated session bursts ("microbursts") under a few realistic configurations. This is intentionally a notes-first artifact — rough numbers, ASCII charts, unresolved questions. Goal is to decide whether we should promote a small change to default prefetch/batching heuristics for Q2 rollout.

Test matrix (scenarios):
1) Baseline: fp16, kv-cache disabled, small-batch=2, windowed-tiling off.
2) KV on: same as baseline but kv-cache enabled (prefetch window 32 tokens).
3) Quantized: int8 quantized serving profile, kv-cache on.
4) Aggressive batch: fp16, kv-cache enabled, small-batch=8, opportunistic windowing on.
5) Edge-region routing: baseline model but routed to nearest edge region (adds variability).

Load profile:
- 5k simulated users over 10 minutes. Each user issues 3–7 short sessions (avg 4) with 1–5 turns each. Burstiness: 20s of concentrated traffic every 60s (approx 3x baseline concurrency during burst).
- Payload: short chat turn (prompt ~40 tokens, expected generation 80 tokens).

Key metrics collected (per scenario):
- p50 latency (ms)
- p95, p99 latency (ms)
- tokens/sec throughput
- dollars-per-1M-tokens (rough estimate using infra unit pricing)
- KV hit rate (when enabled)
- failed requests / retries

Summary table (aggregated numbers, median of 3 runs):
Scenario | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | tps (tokens/s) | $/1M tokens | KV-hit%
Baseline | 120     | 420     | 870     | 9.8           | $3.75       | N/A
KV on    | 110     | 320     | 620     | 11.6          | $3.10       | 43%
Quantized| 130     | 360     | 700     | 12.8          | $2.05       | 41%
AggBatch | 150     | 480     | 920     | 18.7          | $2.00       | 37%
Edge     | 140     | 560     | 1150    | 10.2          | $3.90       | N/A

Quick observations:
- Turning KV cache on reduces tail latency materially (p95/p99 improvement of ~20–30%) and increases tokens/sec because repeated short sessions reuse KV. The KV-hit% around 40% is lower than ideal — suggests our prefetch window or session affinity could be tweaked.
- Quantization reduces infra cost substantially (approx 45% cheaper $/1M tokens vs baseline) while holding p95 close to KV-on. However p50 varies depending on packing efficiency (we saw a 10–15ms jitter increase in some runs).
- Aggressive batching delivers best unit cost but increases median and tail latency: it helps throughput but penalizes microburst latency SLOs. For low-latency applications this is risky.
- Edge routing shows higher variability (worse p99) due to uneven regional capacity and higher cold-start incidence during the concentrated bursts.

ASCII latency-cost frontier (p95 vs $/1M tokens):
(p95 in ms on X axis scaled; $/1M tokens on Y axis)

  $4.0 +-------------------------------------------------+ Edge
      |                    Baseline                    |
  $3.5 |                         *                     |
      |                                               |
  $3.0 |               KV on  *                          |
      |                                               |
  $2.5 |           Quantized *                           |
      |                                               |
  $2.0 |      AggBatch *                                 |
  $1.5 +-------------------------------------------------+ (lower cost, higher p95)
      0ms    200    400    600    800    1000    1200ms

Operational notes / measurement caveats:
- These runs were on a mixed GPU fleet (A100 + some older T4s); per-run variance reflects placement. We should re-run on a homogeneous cluster for a production recommendation.
- The KV hit rate is sensitive to session affinity and how we generate request ids in the load driver. I suspect our driver sometimes rotates session ids leading to artificially low hit% on some runs.
- Network noise: one run had a node-level NIC drop causing a spike in p99 for the Edge scenario. We marked and excluded it from the median but it's evidence that edge regions need more conservative warm pools.

Suggested next actions (short list):
- Immediate: Promote KV-cache as "recommended" for session-heavy low-turn workloads. Update SDK quickstart to enable kv-cache with a note about prefetch-window tuning. (owner: Evan)
- If product wants aggressive cost wins: run focused quantization-only campaign on homogeneous A100 fleet and validate generation quality/eval delta. (owner: Priya)
- Do not default to aggressive batching for low-latency SLAs. Consider a policy that switches to batch-heavy mode only when p50 < 80ms and predicted session length > 10 turns. (owner: Miguel)
- Measurement work: create a reproducible lab run using lab-cluster-phi (ENG-2147) to nail down KV hit causality. Add tests to make sure our load driver preserves session ids. (owner: Ava)

Open questions / risks:
- What is the acceptable tradeoff for customers who care about cost vs p99? Should we expose an explicit "burst-friendly" routing policy in the Console?
- Quality impact of int8 quant: we saw occasional generation truncation artifacts in 2% of samples; need an eval set run.
- Can we increase KV hit% to >60% by changing affinity heuristics? If yes, we could get both cost and latency wins simultaneously.

Links and quick references:
- Load driver job: https://ci.redwood/infer/load-jobs/seq-burst-2026-04-30
- PR for kv-prefetch tuning: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/456
- Jira reference: ENG-2147 (lab cluster repro)

Notes to self: keep this doc light. If team agrees on promoting KV recommendation, I'll draft a short console blurb + SDK snippet. Also add a one-pager for Sales (cost tradeoffs matrix) if we decide to recommend quantized profiles to SMB customers.

End of notes.
